children: Dell Technologies stock was climbing in the Wednesday premarket after the hardware company reported a major earnings and revenue beat that was powered by artificial-intelligence demand.

Dell reported fiscal second-quarter adjusted earnings of $7.04 per share, greatly beating Wall Street estimates of $4.91 per share, according to FactSet. Revenue for the quarter of $47 billion also came in above analyst estimates of $44.9 billion.
In the same period last year, Dell posted adjusted earnings of $2.32 per share on revenue of $29.8 billion.

"IT environments have shifted from cost centers to value drivers that fuel growth and competitive advantage, and customers are investing accordingly-creating opportunity across our portfolio," Jeff Clarke, chief operating officer of Dell, said in the press release.

Clarke added that the clearest sign of these investments is the revenue growth in Dell's AI server business. AI-Optimized Servers revenue was $16.4 billion in the quarter, a 100% increase from the prior year. Dell also exited the quarter with a record $95 billion backlog for the AI server business.
Dell also raised its full-year revenue outlook to $192 billion from $167 billion. That's higher than analyst estimates for revenue of $174 billion.
Shares rose 9.5% in the premarket having also increased following the results.

The bar was high for Dell headed into the report. Shares have soared 238% this year, and are trading at 20.3 times earnings expected over the next 12 months, which is higher than their five-year average of 10.9 times forward earnings. That didn't leave much room for Dell to report anything other than stronger-than-expected results and guidance.
The stock's run comes as Wall Street bets big on the tech hardware firm, whose customers are spending exorbitant amounts to build out the infrastructure needed to power AI.
Other tech hardware companies' earnings in recent weeks point to continued strong demand in the space.
Super Micro Computer posted better-than-expected fiscal fourth-quarter earnings on Aug. 11. The server maker gave a positive outlook for the full fiscal year, citing continued strong demand.
Cisco Systems then also reported solid financials and guidance, with its results boosted by customers' need for AI hardware.
